title: Perform routine operations and identify basic problems in hydroponic systems

lessons.title: Hydroponic systems and daily routines
lessons.html:
What hydroponics is

Hydroponics means growing plants without soil. The roots get water and all their nutrients from a nutrient solution. Plants are often grown in a tunnel or greenhouse. Many South African growers produce tomatoes, cucumbers, peppers, lettuce and herbs this way because yields are high and water use can be well controlled.

Common systems

SystemHow it works
Bag or open system with dripPlants grow in bags of a growing medium such as coir or sawdust; drippers feed nutrient solution several times a day
NFT (nutrient film technique)A thin film of solution flows along channels past the roots, often for lettuce and herbs
Deep water culture / floating raftPlants float on rafts with roots hanging in aerated solution

Main parts of the system

  • Water source and storage tank.
  • Nutrient stock tanks and a mixing or dosing system.
  • Pump, filters, pipes and drippers or channels.
  • Controller or timer that sets irrigation cycles.
  • Meters to measure EC (electrical conductivity, showing nutrient strength) and pH (acidity).

Daily routine

  1. Walk the tunnel. Look at plants, drippers, channels and tanks.
  2. Measure EC and pH of the solution going to the plants and, in bag systems, of the drain water. Record them.
  3. Compare readings with the targets set by the manager for that crop and growth stage.
  4. Check that every dripper is working and the timer is on the right programme.
  5. Check tank levels and top up or mix as instructed.
  6. Record temperature and humidity if there is a gauge.
  7. Train, prune and remove side shoots, old leaves and damaged fruit as instructed for the crop.

Safety

  • Wear gloves and goggles when handling concentrated nutrients and acids. Always add acid to water, never water to acid.
  • Keep electrical connections dry. Report damaged cables at once.

lessons.title: Spotting and reporting problems
lessons.html:
Why problems spread fast

In hydroponics the plants depend completely on the system. In soil, a short dry spell may do little harm; in a bag of coir, a blocked dripper or a pump failure on a hot day can wilt plants within hours. Problems with the solution reach every plant at once. Early detection is your most important job.

System problems

What you seePossible cause
One plant wilting, others fineBlocked or dislodged dripper, root disease
Whole row wiltingBlocked filter, broken pipe, valve closed
No water anywherePump or power failure, empty tank, timer fault
EC much higher or lower than targetDosing error, wrong mixing, tank not topped up
pH outside the target rangeAcid dosing problem, water source change
Algae in channels or tanksLight entering the solution; tanks not covered

Plant problems

  • Yellowing of older leaves – can point to a nutrient shortage such as nitrogen.
  • Brown, burnt leaf edges – can point to salt build-up from EC too high.
  • Blossom end rot on tomatoes – a dark sunken patch at the bottom of the fruit, linked to calcium uptake problems, often made worse by irregular watering.
  • Brown, slimy roots – root rot; healthy roots are white.
  • Pests – whitefly, aphids, thrips, red spider mite, and caterpillars such as Tuta absoluta in tomatoes.

What to do

  1. Fix simple faults you are trained for, such as clearing a blocked dripper.
  2. For pump, power, EC or pH problems, tell the supervisor immediately.
  3. Record what you found, where, when and what you did.
  4. Remove sick plants only if instructed, and wash hands and tools afterwards so disease does not spread.
  5. Keep the tunnel clean: no plant waste on the floor, doors closed, foot bath used.

Key points

  • Hydroponic plants get all water and nutrients from the solution.
  • Measure and record EC and pH daily and compare with targets.
  • Check every dripper; a failure can wilt plants within hours.
  • Learn the signs of system, nutrient, root and pest problems.
  • Report pump, power, EC and pH problems to the supervisor immediately.
